title: Kill-list: macro_* + bbox-macros retire at parity; refactor-atom tier demoted
content: Kill-list extension (refactor v2, supersedes-in-part af3c4783's scope note): The macro_* MCP surface (8 tools) and the bbox-macros planner/registry/expr DSL retire at parity with the rest of the v1 refactor surface — the recipe tier (function store + repo recipes/) is their successor, per refactor-v2-pressure-test §6.6's fold-down mapping. Salvage: the Java emission sidecar and probe→code-nav bindings survive as transform-binding material (§6.5). The refactor-atom tier is demoted: the promotion ladder flattens to improvised cell → recipe; bro_exec with a recipe reference is the external interface, and an atom is minted only when an external consumer earns a standing typed contract, never as a default end state. Nothing retires until the recipe path holds under probes (strangler discipline).
rationale: The macro layer is a declarative programming language built before the real one existed (probes→variables, expr DSL→JS, refusals→bounces, plan/apply two-phase→choke point — v2 §1's diagnosis recurring one level up). The shipped registry is empty in prod, and transcript triage (2026-06-12) found zero real-world invocations of any Java plan kind — there is no consumption to bridge. Operator approved the proposed text 2026-06-12.
